baselineProof.relocation: Exactly four relative imports rewritten to their original module directory

method.environment: Native Chrome155/AMD Radeon ANGLE D3D11,1280x720,DPR1,Yandex S3 dev
method.query: One actual engine frame captures all grid configs, shared density/angular profiles and query arguments. Frozen baseline/current clones compared exactly with actual outputs before/after32 alternating adjacent pairs,8repetitions/sample,6warmup pairs.
method.views: Original belt view and camera translated2engine units (~3990km) right then yaw90deg. Engine stopped for CPU timing, camera/runtime restored afterwards.
method.checks: Public LRU object identity/eviction test passed on unchanged code; temporary real query performance gate fails on unchanged version then passes after optimization. No machine timing or private Map operation assertions in CI.
limits: Local cloned-grid CPU medians, not whole-frame FPS, production performance or other machines.
Motion profile is exploratory with wrapper/query overhead; draw mode outliers do not establish the cause of production spikes.
Exact serialized sector values/order in four captured views; this is not exhaustive pixel parity of all cloud scenes.
Existing finite-index and profile contracts preserved; no new input validation or support for external private cache mutation.
Cloud runner ignores aborted requests; reports zero non-abort asset failures. Full browser archive allows only the named native cancellation test/local held-texture.png/net::ERR_ABORTED triple.
Audit16 remains open for dust/nebula GPU, other sector/visibility CPU, attribute copying and movement spikes.

summary.caveat: 96 real frames; motion=true uses~3990km translation and360-degree camera turn, otherwise stationary. CPU copy/sector/commit wrappers add instrumentation overhead; final run-length snapshot is descriptive, not a paired timing input. Draw mode sums native per-draw GPU queries in RenderPass, excluding volumes/postprocess; frame mode measures full renderFrame separately. Query overhead present. CPU visibility uses browser timer precision. No paired baseline motion or whole-frame speedup claim.
